preamble: Deaffrication with replacement of glottalization by pharyngealization: the ejective affricate [tsʼ] becomes the pharyngealized fricative [sˤ]. Proto-Semitic emphatic *ṣ is reconstructed as an ejective sibilant, most often the affricate *tsʼ (Steiner 1982; Kogan 2011); Geʽez ጸ keeps [tsʼ], while Arabic ṣād and Yemenite Hebrew ṣādē have [sˤ]. Both the ejective value and the affricate onset are reconstructions, so certainty is moderate.

languageExamples.language: Proto-Semitic to Arabic, Hebrew and Aramaic

examples.to: Arabic ʔiṣbaʕ [ʔisˤbaʕ], Biblical Hebrew ʔɛṣbáʕ, Syriac ṣeḇʿā
examples.note: Geʽez አጽባዕት ʾäṣbaʿt keeps [tsʼ]; Amharic ጣት ṭat shows the separate tsʼ > tʼ merger.
Akkadian ṣeḫrum and Ugaritic ṣɣr also have ṣ (Militarev 2006, no. 3075).

examples.to: Arabic ṣāfir [sˤaːfir] (rare) 'kind of small passerine bird', Hebrew ṣippōr 'bird'
